title: WordPress hosting sized to Oracle's free allowance with a shared database container
goal: Run as many agency websites as possible on Oracle's free machine, and write down what it costs beyond that.
why: terraform/modules/oracle-cloud/main.tf asks for 4 OCPU / 24 GB while the Always Free A1 allowance may be 2 OCPU / 12 GB (coordinator note from COST-MODEL); each site runs WordPress 512 MB + its own MariaDB 256 MB (oci-provisioner/src/server.ts); cost model item 6 recommends sharing.
blockedOnOwner: owner decision Q9 (shared database per VM vs multisite)
steps: terraform: instance_ocpus and instance_memory_gb variables defaulting to the free allowance (2 and 12 unless Oracle's current page says 4 and 24; check https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/Content/FreeTier/freetier_topic-Always_Free_Resources.htm with WebFetch and cite the date in WORDPRESS-HOSTING.md); boot volume within the free 200 GB total.

cloud-init: start one shared MariaDB container (docker-compose.shared-db.yml) with a database and user per site created by the provisioner (the provisioner change itself is a follow-up in a later batch if R309 kept per-site MariaDB; document the switch steps here and keep per-site mode working).

docs/ops/WORDPRESS-HOSTING.md: capacity per VM (sites = (RAM - 2 GB) / per-site budget: about 13 with today's 768 MB, about 20 with the shared DB), what happens at the limit (second VM or paid shape and its monthly cost from COST-MODEL 1.10), backups of WordPress volumes, update policy.
terraform fmt and validate (init -backend=false) if terraform is installed.
tests: docker compose -f oci-provisioner/docker-compose.shared-db.yml config (if Docker is installed).
acceptance: Terraform defaults fit the free allowance as documented with a citation.
Capacity and cost beyond it are written down.
gate: terraform -chdir=terraform init -backend=false && terraform -chdir=terraform validate   # skip with a note if terraform is not installed
goLiveVerify: Oracle free-tier capacity availability in ap-mumbai-1 (often out of capacity); real VM boot; site density under load.
notes: Before editing read: this batch file, docs/readiness/READINESS-PLAN.md sections 0 and the design note for this area, desktop/audit/fix/FIX-PLAN.md sections 3-4 (executor rules, worktree bootstrap with node_modules junctions; never npm install inside a worktree unless the batch adds a dependency, and then only in the main checkout by the orchestrator).
Infra only; no backend or provisioner code here.
